assertions.subject: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
assertions.quote: Injuries to the anterior interosseous nerve resulting from direct external trauma do not meet the diagnostic criteria

assertions.subject: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
assertions.predicate: weakness of the muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve
assertions.quote: Only spontaneous cases presenting with weakness of the muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve qualify as true anterior interosseous nerve syndrome

assertions.subject: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
assertions.quote: In contrast to the more gradual onset seen in typical compression syndromes, paralysis in anterior interosseous nerve syndrome often develops suddenly

assertions.subject: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
assertions.quote: paralysis in anterior interosseous nerve syndrome often develops suddenly and resolves spontaneously

assertions.subject: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
assertions.quote: Recurrence remains uncommon, unlike the higher recurrence rates observed in other compressive neuropathies

assertions.subject: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
assertions.quote: Electrodiagnostic studies in many patients with anterior interosseous nerve syndrome reveal a more widespread median motor involvement

assertions.subject: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
assertions.quote: The most frequently identified cause involves an idiopathic immune-mediated neuritis

assertions.subject: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
assertions.quote: An intrinsic compressive lesion in the forearm, including conditions such as compartment syndrome and localized compression neuropathy, represents the second most common etiology
